Thanks for addressing #23529. One regression-test detail from validating the reported behavior: `tests/conftest.py` sets `PREFECT_CLI_WRAP_LINES=False` in the active settings context, so the long-string case does not exercise the wrapping behavior that `get`'s new `soft_wrap=True` fixes. Setting the environment alone also does not override that context.

For a targeted check, use a string longer than 500 characters and wrap the CLI invocation in `with temporary_settings(updates={PREFECT_CLI_WRAP_LINES: True}):`. The CLI runner sets `COLUMNS=500`; then assert `json.loads(result.stdout) == literal_variable.value`. I ran that regression locally: it fails with the original `get` print call and passes with the proposed print kwargs. The other markup/emoji paths are also reproduced against real API/CLI fixtures.

Literal markup/emoji in variable tags is another useful assertion for inspect/list JSON, since those fields go through the same renderer. No global console change is needed.

Disclosure: this validation and review were prepared with Codex assistance; the local regression described above was executed.
